subject.title: Feature Request: Configurable Session Lane Concurrency + Auto-Yield

question: Should OpenClaw add core config for same-session concurrency and automatic yielding, or preserve one active session writer and solve responsiveness through steering, interrupt, and scheduler fairness instead?
rationale: The requested knobs change session-state and public config behavior; source evidence shows the implementation is still missing, but automation should not choose the concurrency, ordering, cancellation, or config contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design scheduler fairness before config
options.body: Keep the issue open and first define foreground/user priority, yielding, abort, and transcript-ordering semantics before exposing any public session-concurrency key.

options.title: Accept a default-off concurrency knob
options.body: Proceed toward a conservative sessionConcurrency-style setting with default 1, explicit upgrade docs, schema/help coverage, and tests for transcript and delivery safety.

options.title: Decline same-session concurrency
options.body: Document the existing steer, interrupt, abort, background exec, and sessions_yield paths as the supported responsiveness model and close or narrow this umbrella.

recommendation.title: Design scheduler fairness before config
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and first define foreground/user priority, yielding, abort, and transcript-ordering semantics before exposing any public session-concurrency key.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest available history on queue/concurrency defaults and the affected command-queue owner boundary.
